codex_workplan.name: Lazy Chat
codex_workplan.scope: This file is an implementation handoff. Its creation does not mean the code has been changed, tested, or deployed. Execute it when instructed to implement this plan. Interpret "the three separately" as three independent tracks: product cards, chat identity and activity, and Printify recommendation priority. Also isolate every product card's image state, including when three cards appear together. Do not create three duplicated chat backends or hardcode a three-product limit.

workspace.rule: Read applicable AGENTS.md instructions and inspect the current diff before editing.
Preserve unrelated work, authentication, explicit CORS allowlists, rate limiting, cart behavior, prices, and checkout links.
Keep credentials server-side. Add no runtime dependencies without a demonstrated need.
Use codex/ branch names and separate commits for each change unit below.
Branch each unit from the latest accepted baseline. Integrate and release one unit at a time; do not overwrite previously accepted changes with an older branch deployment.
Separate branches isolate changes; runtime isolation requires the component boundaries specified below.

evidence.local_fact: Local extension name is chat-bubble. The reported published name lazy-customs-chat-agent-3 must be reconciled with the selected Shopify app, extension UID, and deployed version before release.
The card reads product.image_url. Its onerror assigns the same remote Shopify placeholder without removing the handler, allowing repeated failure requests.

The normalizer already sets image_url from product.image_url or the URL of the first product.media entry whose type equals image. The actual live catalog field is not established by this inspection; capture it before changing the mapping. Both structuredContent.products and content[0].text products are supported locally.

Header uses the chat.title translation. en.default.json currently says Store Assistant. The block already exposes welcome_message and passes it through window.shopChatConfig. chat.js contains three fallback greeting occurrences, including history and reset paths. The pasted v1.0 claim that configuration is not read does not match this checkout.

Actual nesting is systemPrompts.standardAssistant.content and systemPrompts.systemShopping.content, with systemDesignCoach and enthusiasticAssistant also present. Guardrails are text within prompts, not a separate top-level guardrails key. AppConfig defaults to standardAssistant, and the extension schema currently offers standardAssistant and enthusiasticAssistant. Editing systemShopping alone would not reliably change default storefront behavior.
evidence.missing_asset: The attachment supplied for this handoff contains pasted-text.txt only, not lazy-chat-hub-source.png. No matching hub PNG, SVG, or JPG was found in the filename search of this workspace. The text describes a central square connected to eight surrounding nodes; it is not the image itself. Locate the actual source or request it for an exact recolor. Do not claim to have inspected or recolored it. Continue the other independent changes while this asset is unavailable.

change.diagnosis: Capture a sanitized, read-only search_catalog response and, if needed, get_product response using the actual discovered tool schema. Trace one product from raw catalog data through processProductSearchResult, the product_results stream event, and createCard to the final img.src. Record the exact raw field path and where image data is lost. Do not guess fields or scrape assistant prose for image URLs. Do not place orders or create carts to diagnose images.
change.contract: Normalize each product to its own stable identity, existing commerce fields, and image_url. image_url is a validated HTTPS product-image URL, or an empty string when absent. Preserve the existing client-facing image_url field; keep schema-specific mapping on the server. Support only shapes demonstrated by actual responses or documented tool schemas. If search lacks images, use an existing supported detail lookup with bounded work and caching; one lookup failure must not discard sibling products. Preserve search order and product identity.

implementation.step: Correct the source request or normalizer where evidence shows the field is lost. Preserve existing supported response envelopes.
Render each card from that product's image_url. Never share mutable image, fallback, loading, or error state across cards.
Remove the remote placeholder URL from product rendering entirely. Use a bundled local asset or inline SVG fallback with no external resource references.
Install the error handler before assigning src. On the first error, detach the handler before applying the fallback. A fallback failure is terminal.
For an absent URL, render the local fallback directly. Do not send a request to an empty src.
Keep stable card identity during streaming or updates; do not recreate failed images or reassign unchanged src values on every text chunk.
Bound failure state to the current product and image URL. Reset it only when the actual URL changes or a new conversation begins.
Set dimensions or aspect-ratio and suitable object-fit; use the product title as alternative text. Preserve product links and Add to Cart.

acceptance.check: With a captured catalog fixture containing real images, assert the normalizer and product_results event preserve the exact expected image URLs.
Render three distinct products: one valid image, one forced HTTP 503 image, and one absent image. Only the failed and absent cards use fallback; the valid card remains visible and interactive.
Force fallback failure too. After repeated stream updates, request counts remain bounded: at most one failed-source attempt and one fallback assignment per unchanged card URL per conversation.
Ask for shirts and totes in a fresh chat. Check each card against its catalog product; no card with a valid loading image uses fallback.
Observe the Network panel for at least 30 seconds after rendering and through another reply: zero requests to placeholder-images-image_large.png, no retry loop, and no image-related flicker.
Run targeted regression tests for normalization and isolated failure behavior, then the app's existing npm test and npm run build checks.

track.name: Chat identity, greeting, and activity

change.implementation: Add a merchant-editable assistant_name text setting in chat-interface.liquid with default Lazy Chat and label Assistant name. Render it safely with Liquid escaping and a Lazy Chat fallback. Reconcile the existing chat.title locale fallback so Store Assistant cannot leak into the intended header. Set the active theme's saved value where required; a schema default does not overwrite an existing merchant setting. Do not modify unrelated merchant copy.

acceptance.check: In the active theme editor, Assistant name is available and set to Lazy Chat.
After release and refresh, desktop and mobile headers read exactly Lazy Chat with no clipping.

change.copy: Heyyy… what can I help you find today?
change.implementation: Use the existing welcome_message setting as the configurable source. Update its schema default and all three chat.js fallback occurrences consistently, preferably through one small greeting accessor. Update the active theme's saved default greeting as needed. Interpret "spoken in a lazy way" as relaxed written delivery; this change adds no audio playback or speech service. Keep the greeting short, with no emoji.

acceptance.check: Fresh open, empty history, history-fetch failure, and New Chat/reset all display the chosen greeting once.
No new greeting displays Hi there. Do not rewrite old conversation messages containing historical copy.
The existing merchant setting still overrides the default correctly.

change.asset_requirement: Use the actual brown hub source once available. Recolor it to the active storefront's verified theme colors with a transparent background, preserving its geometry. Reuse actual theme tokens or expose merchant-editable color settings tied to verified values. Do not treat the approximate teal/indigo values in v1.0 as confirmed brand colors. Put the finished asset in extensions/chat-bubble/assets. If source remains missing, report only this change blocked; do not invent or silently substitute a different logo.

implementation.step: Place the hub beside the header title, about 28–40 px. Give a decorative image empty alt text because the adjacent name already identifies the assistant.
Use CSS keyframes for a lazy clockwise idle turn of about 10 seconds. During response processing, use about 2 seconds per turn; counterclockwise or alternating direction is optional.

Connect an avatar-only is-active class to the real request lifecycle alongside showTypingIndicator and hideTypingIndicator. Cover completion, errors, cancellation, timeout, authentication handoff, and reset.
If requests can overlap, derive activity from pending request identity or a count so one completion cannot incorrectly mark another active request idle.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop rotation completely and retain a nonmoving activity cue. Avoid per-frame JavaScript timers.
Missing avatar markup or an asset failure must not break sending messages, rendering cards, or checkout.

acceptance.check: Inspect the actual asset at desktop and mobile size: correct hub geometry, verified brand colors, no brown, transparent background, and readable title.
Send a message and verify idle-to-active-to-idle transitions, including a forced backend error and cancellation/reset.
Emulate reduced motion and verify zero rotation with a visible static activity cue.
Break a product image while a reply streams: avatar activity and healthy cards continue independently.

change.intent: Printify is the preferred provider for default and proactive product offers. This is a recommendation-priority change, not a migration of existing fulfillment, an order-routing change, or an enrollment in the separately named Printify Choice service. Do not claim all products ship worldwide or that every destination is supported.

implementation.step: Trace the storefront's actual prompt_type through the request and selected provider. Apply the policy to every supported shopping entry point, including the active default; do not edit only an unused prompt.
Keep the persona calm and concise and identify it as Lazy Chat where appropriate. Preserve existing policy and checkout formatting instructions.

Inspect the live catalog tool schema. If supported, prefer a verified Printify vendor filter or the verified Printify collection for generic and proactive queries; do not invent filter parameters or collection IDs.
Retain trusted provider metadata for ranking where available. A store vendor label may support catalog grouping; do not present it as proof of actual fulfillment routing or destination coverage.
For ordinary category requests, lead with relevant Printify items. Relevance, availability, explicit product choices, budget, and customer constraints take precedence over provider preference.

If relevant Printify results are empty or insufficient, broaden once to eligible alternatives and deduplicate by stable identity. Provider-filter errors also get a bounded fallback, never an infinite retry.
If filtering is unavailable but provider metadata exists, rank relevant Printify items before applying the display limit. Keep assistant recommendations and card order consistent.
If neither filtering nor reliable metadata is available, report that limitation and the exact missing capability; do not guess fulfillment providers from product titles.
Honor explicit requests for other providers or exact products. Use catalog-backed prices and capabilities; do not invent shipping guarantees, partnerships, availability, or exclusivity.
Do not alter Printify credentials, fulfillment clients, existing orders, payments, or publication settings as part of recommendation priority.

acceptance.check: In fresh conversations, What do you have? and Show me shirts lead with relevant verified Printify items when available, in both assistant text and cards.
An explicit non-Printify product or provider request is respected and not replaced with unrelated Printify stock.
A category with no matching Printify results returns relevant alternatives through one bounded broadening attempt.
Unavailable or unsuitable Printify stock does not outrank suitable products solely due to provider.
Exercise the actual default prompt and systemShopping path. Assert that neither output claims exclusive fulfillment or guaranteed worldwide delivery.
Run targeted policy/ranking regression checks plus npm test and npm run build from the app directory.

release_and_evidence.sequence: images, name, greeting, hub when its asset is available, then printify. The missing hub must not prevent the Printify change from proceeding.
release_and_evidence.step: Before implementation, verify local versus deployed versions and record the baseline commit. Before release, verify the target app/store and backend service from current configuration.

For each unit, record exact changed files and runnable commands or reproducible browser steps, exit codes, and results. Add focused tests for behavioral defects; simple copy edits need direct verification.

Release extension changes using shopify app deploy from shop-chat-agent-main once the unit is validated and release is authorized by the executing session. Record the actual extension release/version.

For a backend mapping or recommendation change, verify and redeploy the intended Railway service; valiant-liberation is a supplied project reference that must be checked. Record the deployed commit and deployment ID.
When images require both backend and widget changes, keep the image_url contract compatible and deploy the backend first, then the widget. Recheck both together.
Refresh the actual storefront and run that unit's acceptance checks plus a smoke check of message sending, product cards, and cart controls. Do not submit a purchase.
Rollback only the failing unit using its previous verified extension version or backend deployment as appropriate. Verify other accepted units still work.
release_and_evidence.report: For each unit return: status, branch and commit, files changed, raw image field and normalized field where relevant, tests executed and results, storefront evidence, deployment identifiers, and unresolved blockers. Mark unrun checks not run. Never describe planned checks as passed.
